requirements.businessContext: Module 07 exposes the public standings READ endpoint (`GET /api/standings`) and the standings-shaping logic that aggregates already-persisted GW results into ranked tables. It covers three computation paths — TVT league-stage standings, Triple Crown PL standings (38 GWs, no bonus margin, leaguePoints stored authoritatively by the GW processor), and JPL Auction standings (pure cumulative-points race with payout history and squad-value tie-breakers). It also serves the rank-change indicator, the CBP tooltip (chips / bonus points / hit penalty), the qualification-zone legend used by the standings UI, and the Redis-backed page cache that fronts the response. The WRITE side (computing match points, bonus, payouts during GW processing) lives in module 05; UI rendering is module 17; playoffs are module 08; cup-group standings detail is deferred to module 09.

businessRules.rule: `leagueSlug` query parameter is REQUIRED — endpoint returns 400 `{ error: 'leagueSlug parameter is required' }` when missing.
An unknown `leagueSlug` returns 404 `{ error: 'League not found' }`; the route does not infer or default to any league.

League stage end is `38` for Triple Crown leagues and `playoffStartGw - 1` for all other formats; fixtures with `gameweek.number > leagueStageEnd` are excluded from W/D/L, points-for, bonus, and chip aggregation.
Only fixtures with `competitionType === 'pl'` or NULL `competitionType` count toward PL standings; cup-group, UCL-knockout and UEL-knockout fixtures are skipped.
Ghost teams (`isGhost === true`) are excluded from PL standings via `allTeams.filter(t => !t.isGhost)`.
TVT `leaguePoints` are computed as `(wins * 2) + (draws * 1) + cbpPoints - hitPenaltyTotal` where `cbpPoints = chipPoints + bonusPoints`.
Triple Crown `leaguePoints` is read directly from `teams.leaguePoints` (stored authoritatively by `processTripleCrownGameweek`); the standings route does NOT recompute it.
W/D/L are derived from RAW FPL scores (`result.homeScore` vs `result.awayScore`), NOT from chip-adjusted match points.
Bonus points are awarded as 1 point per qualifying fixture, doubled to 2 when `homeUsedDoublePointer`/`awayUsedDoublePointer` is set on the result row.
Hit penalty: each GW in which ANY player on the team took strictly more than 12 raw FPL transfer hits contributes −1 to `leaguePoints` (one deduction per qualifying GW, not per player).

Hit-penalty data for processed GWs is loaded from Redis (`getAllCachedScores`) first; on cache miss the route fetches per-player GW scores from FPL in parallel within each GW (GW loop sequential to bound concurrency).

If the FPL hit-penalty fetch throws (FPL outage / rate-limit), the route logs the error and returns standings WITHOUT hit deductions rather than 500-ing — partial correctness is preferred over total failure.
Triple Crown leagues SKIP the FPL hit-penalty fetch entirely because hit penalties are already baked into the stored `leaguePoints`.

GET /api/standings sorts teams within each group using the canonical TVT 4-tier tiebreaker: 1) Overall Points (leaguePoints) DESC, 2) Max Wins DESC, 3) Head-to-Head match points DESC (the points each team earned against the other using W=2/D=1/L=0), 4) Bonus Points DESC. Matches the spec at src/lib/formats/tvt/scoring.ts:215-246. The previously-used pointsFor and cbpPoints tiers are no longer part of the sort.

GET /api/standings response.teams[i].bonusPoints reflects the stored teams.bonusPoints column. The previously-exposed calculatedBonus field has been removed (was a per-request fixture sweep that could disagree with the stored ledger after manual edits or missed processor updates). Single source of truth.
Standings response groups teams by `group.name` (excluding any group whose name starts with `cup-`, case-insensitive); groupless leagues collapse all teams into `groupA` with an empty `groupB`.
Within each group, ranks are 1-based by sort order and assigned to both `rank` and `groupRank` fields on each team row.
Qualification zone: teamSize=8 → ranks 1–4 `playoffs`, 5–8 `eliminated` (no challenger); teamSize=16 or 32 → ranks 1–8 `playoffs`, 9–14 `challenger`, 15+ `eliminated`.

GET /api/standings response.legend is teamSize-aware. For 8-team leagues: { top4: 'TVT Title Play-offs', rank5to8: 'Eliminated' } (matching getQualificationZone: top-4 playoffs, ranks 5-8 eliminated, no challenger). For 16- or 32-team leagues: { top8: 'TVT Title Play-offs', rank9to14: 'Challenger Series', rank15to16: 'Eliminated' } as before.
Previous-GW rank snapshot uses the SAME sort keys as the current pass (`leaguePoints` → `pointsFor` → `cbpPoints`) computed against all league-stage fixtures up to but not including `maxPlayedGw`.
`previousRank` and `rankDelta` are only populated when `maxPlayedGw > 1`; otherwise both fields are `null` on every team row.
`rankDelta = previousRank − currentRank` (positive = climbed, negative = dropped, zero = unchanged); is `null` when previous rank is unknown.
Rank-change indicator is display-only and never influences playoff seeding, zone assignment, or group order; TVT playoff bracket generation uses its own helper in `tvt/playoffs.ts`.

CBP tooltip enumerates exactly 6 chip entries (2 sets × 3 enabled chip codes) with set boundaries `[1, ceil(leagueStageEnd/2)]` and `[ceil(leagueStageEnd/2)+1, leagueStageEnd]`; the 3 chip codes come from `leagues.enabledChips` (default `["D","W","C"]`).

Each CBP tooltip chip entry has `status` ∈ {`available` (no chip row), `used` (`isProcessed=true`), `pending` (row exists but not processed)} and carries `points` (0 when available), `gameweek` (when used/pending) and `opponent` (only for Challenge Chip).
`chipPoints` accumulates only chips with `isProcessed=true`; a `C` (Challenge) chip is always summed (including 0-point rows) while any other chip type is summed only when `pointsAwarded > 0`.
Chips with `gameweek.number > leagueStageEnd` (i.e. playoff GWs) are excluded from `chipPoints` and from previous-GW chip totals.
JPL Auction standings: ranking is `totalPoints DESC` → `squadValue ASC` (lower wins) → `purse DESC` (higher wins); ranks are 1-based, no groups.

Auction `squadValue` is the sum of FMV of every actively-owned player, where FMV uses RAW points only (`rawPoints`, falling back to legacy `points`) — synergy bonus never compounds into FMV/squad value.
Auction `totalPoints` for a team = `Σ rawPoints + Σ synergyBonus + Σ clubResultBonus` across all GWs the team has been scored.

Auction `previousRank`/`rankDelta` are computed using cumulative points through `maxGw - 1`, with the same secondary keys; teams with no GW history at `previousGw` get `previousRank=null` and `rankDelta=null`.
FMV appreciation tiers: 0–100 raw points → £20K/pt, 100–200 → £40K/pt, 200+ → £60K/pt; negative raw points are clamped to 0 before tier accumulation.
PL Club Auction display: if a team owns a PL club, the response replaces `teamName` with the owned club's `plTeamName` from `auctionClubOwnership`.
Auction `currentGwNumber` = max(highest scored GW, FPL `is_current`/`is_next` event id); on FPL fetch failure it stays at the highest scored GW.

Auction live-club-result branch (`currentGwNumber > maxScoredGw && currentGwNumber > 0`) computes the in-progress `liveClubResultByTeam` for every owned club; the response is NOT written to the Redis cache during the live branch to prevent stale scorelines.
Legacy `clubResultSummary` rows (null in DB) are backfilled on-the-fly via `backfillClubSummaries` so the standings tooltip shows a real fixture string instead of em-dash.

GET /api/standings caches the FULL (unfiltered) standings payload per leagueId. When a `group` query parameter is supplied, BOTH the cache read and the cache write are skipped — the response is computed fresh from the DB and never written back. This prevents (a) returning the wrong group's slice from a cached unfiltered payload, and (b) a group-filtered response from poisoning the slot for subsequent unfiltered callers. Cache-key shape in fpl-cache.ts is unchanged.
Cache writes are fire-and-forget (`.catch(() => {})`) and never block or fail the response.

GET /api/standings catch block returns HTTP 500 with body { error: string, detail: string }. The magic-defaults stub ({ groupA:[], groupB:[], leagueStageEnd:30, teamSize:32, groupsRevealed:false }) is gone — it masked real server errors by serving them as 200 OK. Empty-league cases (no fixtures yet) are handled in the happy path and return 200 with the league's real teamSize/leagueStageEnd.
`groupsRevealed` flag is sourced from `settings` row with `key='groupsRevealed'`, value compared as the literal string `'true'`; absence ⇒ false.

Cup-group standings tie-break (computed by `computeCupGroupStandings`): `cupGroupPoints DESC`, then goal-difference (GF − GA) DESC, then `goalFor` DESC. (Detailed cup-group rules deferred to module 09.)

defects.title: PL standings tiebreaker diverges from documented 4-tier rule (missing max-wins and head-to-head)
defects.description: The `/api/standings` route sorts teams by `leaguePoints DESC → pointsFor DESC → cbpPoints DESC` (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:616-620). However the TVT scoring spec at src/lib/formats/tvt/scoring.ts:215-246 defines the league-stage tiebreaker as 1) Overall Points, 2) Max Wins, 3) Head-to-Head, 4) Bonus Points. Neither `wins`, `headToHeadRecord`, nor `bonusPoints` are used by the standings sort. Two teams tied on league points and points-for will be ordered by chips+bonus, which can flip the documented ranking.
defects.expectedBehaviour: The sort should match `compareTiebreaker` in tvt/scoring.ts — after leaguePoints, break ties by max wins, then head-to-head record, then bonus points.
defects.actualBehaviour: Sort uses `pointsFor` then `cbpPoints` and ignores wins, H2H, and (stored) bonus points entirely. The previous-GW snapshot sort at route.ts:459-463 has the same divergence.
defects.notes: Options: (a) replace the standings sort with `compareTiebreaker` from tvt/scoring.ts (requires materialising W and H2H records here); (b) update the spec to match the simpler sort if product owner approves. Risk: any cup-tied podium decided by current sort may be product-incorrect. Cross-check with playoffs.ts which uses its own `getGroupStandings`. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean. [QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-27 — pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-27 — BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Standings sort now uses the canonical 4-tier TVT tiebreaker from src/lib/formats/tvt/scoring.ts:215-246: leaguePoints DESC -> wins DESC -> head-to-head match points DESC -> bonusPoints DESC. Each TeamStanding now carries a `headToHeadRecord: Record<opponentTeamId, matchPts>` built during the fixture loop (W=2, D=1, L=0 against each opponent). The field is internal-only — toResponseRow strips it before serialization so the public API shape is unchanged. Replaces the previous (leaguePoints, pointsFor, cbpPoints) sort that diverged from the documented rule.

defects.title: Standings legend block is hard-coded and inaccurate for 8-team leagues
defects.description: The standings response always emits `legend: { top8: 'TVT Title Play-offs', rank9to14: 'Challenger Series', rank15to16: 'Eliminated' }` (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:667-671). For a `teamSize=8` league, ranks 9–14 and 15–16 do not exist and the actual cutoff for playoffs is top-4 (per `getQualificationZone` at line 697-705), so the legend is misleading.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Legend should be derived from `teamSize` and `getQualificationZone` (e.g. `{ top4: 'Playoffs', rank5to8: 'Eliminated' }` for 8-team leagues) or omitted in favour of UI-side computation.
defects.actualBehaviour: All leagues — including 8-team and Triple Crown — receive the 32-team legend, so UI components that key off these strings render incorrect bands.
defects.notes: Low risk for the 16/32-team flagship leagues; cosmetic but actively wrong for 8-team variants. Fix is local to this route — branch on `leagueTeamSize`. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean. [QA-VERIFIED] Pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Made the standings response legend format-aware (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:664-686). For teamSize=8 leagues the legend now uses {top4, rank5to8} matching getQualificationZone's 8-team rule. For 16/32-team leagues the legend keeps the existing {top8, rank9to14, rank15to16} shape. Consumers can branch on the keys present in `legend`.

defects.title: Redis standings cache key ignores `group` filter so cached payloads bleed across group views
defects.description: `getCachedStandings`/`setCachedStandings` use the key `standings:v2:{leagueId}` (src/lib/fpl-cache.ts:365-378). The standings route applies the `group` query param AFTER the cache lookup (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:102-108 vs 332-335), so a payload cached from an unfiltered request is returned verbatim to a caller asking for `?group=B`, and vice-versa. The cache also does not key on `leagueSlug` vs `leagueId` aliasing.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Either skip the cache when a `group` filter is present, or include the group token in the cache key (`standings:v2:{leagueId}:group=B`).
defects.actualBehaviour: First requester wins the cache slot; subsequent requesters with different `group` filters receive the wrong slice until TTL expiry.
defects.notes: Trivial fix; bump cache version (STANDINGS_CACHE_VERSION) when shipping. Impact today is minimal because the UI generally doesn't pass `group`, but any deep-link that does will be broken. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean for touched files, manual diff review clean. Awaiting QA re-run of TC-STAND-052. [QA] Re-run TC-STAND-052 — the second response (with ?group=B) should now bypass the cache and return only group-B teams; expected behaviour now matches AC-STAND-039 (after inversion to confirm the fix). [BA] BR-STAND-038 / AC-STAND-039 text should be updated: cache reads AND writes are now skipped when a `group` filter is present (chose bypass over a group-suffixed key because group-filtered requests are rare and a per-group key would fragment the cache). [QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-26 — pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-26 — BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Gated both the cache read (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:104-115) and the TVT cache write (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:693-699) on `!group`. When a group filter is present the route now bypasses Redis on both sides, so a filtered response cannot poison the unfiltered slot and an unfiltered cached entry cannot be served to a filtered caller. Chose bypass over a group-suffixed key because group-filtered requests are uncommon and a separate key would fragment the cache for negligible benefit.

defects.title: Top-level catch returns HTTP 200 with stub payload, masking real errors
defects.description: Any exception thrown during standings computation is swallowed and the response is HTTP 200 with `{ groupA: [], groupB: [], leagueStageEnd: 30, teamSize: 32, groupsRevealed: false }` (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:680-690). This hides DB failures, drizzle relational errors, transient FPL/cache issues, and prevents Sentry/UI from differentiating a real outage from a brand-new league with no fixtures. The defaulted `leagueStageEnd: 30` / `teamSize: 32` also leak even for 8-team leagues.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Return a 500-class status (or distinguish 'empty league' from 'computation failed') and surface error telemetry. The narrow case of 'no fixtures yet' should be detected explicitly, not modelled as a catch-all.
defects.actualBehaviour: All errors collapse to a single 200/empty shape with magic defaults that misrepresent league configuration.
defects.notes: Risk: silent regressions during deploys; on-call sees no alerts. Suggested fix: tighten the catch to known empty-state cases or return `{ status: 500, error }` for unknown failures. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean for touched files, manual diff review clean. Awaiting QA re-run of TC-STAND-053. [QA] Re-run TC-STAND-053 — a DB error injected inside the standings computation should now produce HTTP 500 with body `{ error: 'Failed to compute standings', detail: <message> }`, not the old 200/stub. The 'no fixtures yet' case is handled organically by the happy path (empty groups with the league's real teamSize/leagueStageEnd) and never reaches the catch. [BA] BR-STAND-040 / AC-STAND-040 must be rewritten: the catch now returns HTTP 500 with `{ error, detail }`, and the magic defaults (leagueStageEnd:30, teamSize:32, groupsRevealed:false) are gone. AC-STAND-040 currently asserts the stub shape and must be inverted. [QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-26 — pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-26 — BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Replaced the swallow-all catch with a proper HTTP 500 response carrying `{ error: 'Failed to compute standings', detail: <message> }` (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:697-709). The defaulted 32/30 stub is gone — the empty-league case is handled organically by the happy path (zero teams produces empty groupA/groupB with the league's real teamSize and leagueStageEnd, so it never hits the catch). Server errors are now visible to clients and monitoring.

defects.title: Response carries both stored `bonusPoints` and recomputed `calculatedBonus`, which can drift
defects.description: The standings team row exposes `bonusPoints: team.bonusPoints` (the stored value from `teams.bonusPoints`) AND `calculatedBonus: bonusPtsTotal` (the value derived from the current fixture+result sweep). When `teams.bonusPoints` was never updated by the GW processor, was edited manually, or was reset during a partial season-reset, these two fields can disagree — yet `leaguePoints` is computed from the calculated value while the UI may read either field.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Pick ONE source of truth (almost certainly the recomputed `bonusPtsTotal`) and either remove the other field or make them provably equal.
defects.actualBehaviour: Both fields are returned, downstream consumers can disagree about a team's bonus total, and the leaguePoints math silently uses the calculated value regardless of the stored one.
defects.notes: Audit: confirm whether `teams.bonusPoints` is still maintained anywhere (search GW-processing in module 05). If unused, drop the column or stop returning the field. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean. [QA-VERIFIED] Pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Removed `calculatedBonus` from the /api/standings response (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:600-605) AND from the TeamStanding interface (src/app/api/standings/route.ts:38-56). bonusPoints (the stored teams.bonusPoints column) is now the single source of truth. The recomputed value was a drift hazard whenever the GW processor missed an update.
